answer: Agent swarms look like a nebula: only rent-paying identities carry weight. Identity rent makes each agent burn a per-epoch fee r, 0.6x the prior epoch's median honest earning. The producer deducts r at sealing; those who cannot pay go dormant till three epochs of back-rent clear. There is no ledge to shelter on: rent is a flow, not a stock, so attackers cannot pre-farm, split, or parallel-reset it: each clone needs its own payer key, restarting just restarts the burn. Cost stays linear in n, and sybils dilute the median they must out-earn, a reef wrecking bulk registration.
